briefdescription.para: Type-erased interface for service-entity (clinic, pharmacy, laboratory, radiology center) CRUD+S operations.

detaileddescription.para: In everyday language, this file lists the jobs every "service entity" (a clinic, a pharmacy, a laboratory or a radiology center) must be able to do. Those jobs are: Create a new one, Read one, Update one, Delete one, and Search through many — together called "CRUD+S". "Type-erased" is a fancy word for hiding the exact type: the rest of the server can call these jobs without knowing which kind of entity is actually behind them. Each job appears twice: an ordinary version that reports its result through a callback (a "call me when you are done" function), and an "async" version that uses a coroutine (a function that can pause and resume later). This file only declares the jobs; the real work is written in the class that inherits from this one.

WHY THIS FILE MATTERS IN THE SERVER: This is the doorway the HTTP routing layer uses to reach every service controller. Because all the job functions here are "virtual", one single route handler can serve clinics, pharmacies, laboratories and radiology centers without knowing which one it is talking to — the call is automatically forwarded to the right concrete controller. This file calls into nothing itself, but it is called by the services route registry and it is the contract that ServiceController fulfils. Without it, every route would need separate code for each entity type and adding a new service type would mean rewriting the routes.

CONCEPTS TO LEARN (for beginners):
Virtual functions (calling the right version through a base pointer): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/virtual
C++20 coroutines (functions that pause and resume with co_await/co_return): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/coroutines
C++20 concepts / requires (compile-time checks on template arguments): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/constraints
